rationale: The golden submission is rejected by evaluate.py because the golden's own reported behavior does not match what the shipped RTL actually does when simulated: FR2 fails (golden claims mismatch_at_zero_verdict='mismatch' but the RTL, when traced/simulated per the testbench, yields 'match'), and SR2 fails (golden's cycle_relationship formula k+2 does not predict the measured cycle counts; measured cycles for even k are 17, not matching a clean linear model). Tracing the actual inputs/signature_compare.v RTL: the early-exit else-if branch fires only when byte_count != 15, and because byte_count is only checked/incremented under byte_valid with a subtle interaction between mismatch_found latching and the terminal check, the real simulated behavior diverges from both the hidden_spec.ground_truth formula (k+2) and the golden's report content. This is not an evaluator bug (no traceback, clean FR/SR FAIL against actual simulated behavior) and the evaluation contract explicitly allows/expects iverilog cross-checks against the real RTL. The root inconsistency is between the shipped RTL implementation and the hidden ground truth / golden report describing it -- i.e. the input artifact (signature_compare.v) does not implement the intended monotonic early-exit timing leak the spec and golden assume. This matches the analyzer's own diagnosis of a parity/off-by-one bug in the RTL's byte_count/mismatch_found interaction. Per the golden_rejected rule, since the golden's claims do not match the actual (correct-per-spec) behavior of a properly implemented early-exit comparator, the case_artifacts (specifically the RTL and/or the golden report and testbench-derived ground truth) must be regenerated so that the RTL genuinely implements the k+2 monotonic relationship described in hidden_spec.ground_truth, and the golden report is regenerated to match verified simulation output.
revision_instructions: Regenerate inputs/signature_compare.v so its actual synchronous behavior, when driven by inputs/testbench_harness.v via iverilog/vvp, produces the exact monotonic timing relationship described in hidden_spec.ground_truth: cycles_to_done = k + 2 for a mismatch at 0-indexed byte position k (k=0..15), and 17 or 18 cycles (per the same formula applied to k=15/full-match, consistent and verified by actual simulation) for the full-match case, with FR1 (full match verdict='match') and FR2 (mismatch at position 0 verdict='mismatch') holding true when simulated. Concretely: trace through the byte_count increment timing and the mismatch_found/done assertion logic for EVERY byte position (0 through 15) by hand or via an internal verification script before shipping, confirming there is no parity-dependent or off-by-one bug that causes some byte positions (e.g. even k) to behave differently from others (e.g. odd k) -- all 16 mismatch positions plus the full-match case must show a single consistent linear (or otherwise simply describable) relationship between mismatch position and cycles-to-done, with no discontinuities. After the RTL is corrected and independently verified via simulation, regenerate golden/vulnerability_report.json so every field (baseline_behavior verdicts, cycle_relationship formula/slope/intercept, early_exit_signal identification, constant_time_fix, proposed_fix_preserves_correctness) is derived from and matches the actual measured simulation output of the corrected RTL against the reference testbench, not from an assumed or previously drafted formula. Add a mandatory internal preflight step (before shipping) that runs evaluate.py against the regenerated golden report and requires all FR/SR checks to PASS; do not ship the case until this preflight is green.', validate this end-to-end before resubmitting for arbitration."},
